title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: pages 1-67 of the 'Longue Marche' manuscripts, after Conjectures B/B' (the section conjecture for hyperbolic curves over fields K finitely generated over Q, together with a fixed-point form on the completed Poincaré covering). On this page Grothendieck spreads the conjecture out over an arithmetic base.

Setting.
- K is the function field of a model S: a normal, presumably regular, scheme of finite type over Z or Q, 'satisfying a certain condition'.
- U_K is a hyperbolic curve that extends to a relative hyperbolic curve U_S -> S, with compactification \hat U_S and cusp divisor S' = \hat U_S \ U_S, finite étale over S.
- E denotes the arithmetic fundamental groups: E_S = pi_1(S) and E_{U_S} = pi_1(U_S).

The extension (4). The homotopy exact sequence gives 1 -> pi -> E_{U_S} -> E_S -> 1, where pi is the geometric fundamental group of a fibre. This needs tameness or characteristic-0 fibres for the full profinite pi, a point the page does not address.

The cartesian square (5). Since S is normal, E_K = Gal(\bar K/K) -> E_S is surjective. The fibre-product diagram says E_{U_K} = E_{U_S} x_{E_S} E_K, with the same kernel pi.

Consequence.
- Sections of E_{U_K} -> E_K are the same as continuous lifts E_K -> E_{U_S} of the surjection E_K -> E_S.
- Among these lifts, those trivial on ker(E_K -> E_S) = pi_1 of the generic point relative to S factor through E_S. These are exactly the sections of (4), i.e. the 'unramified over S' sections.

Next page: the section conjecture then predicts exactly two kinds of sections of (4).
1. Those from K-points of U_K that extend to regular sections S -> U_S. Grothendieck still has to check that a merely rational section gives a splitting of (4) only if it is regular.
2. Cuspidal ones, from K-rational cusps, i.e. sections S -> S'. Here it remains to decide when such a cusp yields a non-empty packet of splittings of (4), and to describe all of them.

In modern terms this is the 'section conjecture over a base' or 'integral/unramified section conjecture': S-integral points correspond to Galois sections unramified along S.
errors: No outright error. Two points are implicit or unverified.

Exactness of 1 -> pi -> pi_1(U_S) -> pi_1(S) -> 1 with the full profinite geometric pi needs the cusps to be étale over S and the fibre fundamental groups to behave well (e.g. S over Q, or restriction to prime-to-p/tame parts). With S of finite type over Z this needs qualification, presumably the 'certaine condition' on the model.

The claim (next page) that a rational section defines a splitting of (4) only if it is regular is plausible for regular S, but is left 'à vérifier'. It follows from Zariski–Nagata purity plus the extension of rational maps into schemes containing no rational curves, which hyperbolic curves satisfy, with care in mixed characteristic. Without regularity of S it can fail.

Cuspidal sections need not all descend to S. The obstruction involves the normal bundle/Kummer class of the cusp section, i.e. the tame tubular-neighbourhood extension of pi_1(S) by Z^(1). The page only raises this question.

ideas.what: Spreading out the section conjecture over a model S: E_{U_K} is the pullback of the extension pi_1(U_S) -> pi_1(S) along the surjection G_K -> pi_1(S).
ideas.modern_name: base change of the fundamental exact sequence; relative / 'over a base' section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1983 letter to Faltings, standard folklore); systematised in Stix, 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups' (LNM 2054)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. XIII (homotopy exact sequence); the letter to Faltings (1983) states the section conjecture for finitely generated fields

ideas.what: Splittings of pi_1(U_S) -> pi_1(S) correspond to Galois sections of U_K that are trivial on the inertia/kernel of G_K -> pi_1(S).
ideas.modern_name: unramified (integral) Galois sections; section conjecture for integral points
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; discussed by Stix and others in the context of integral points

ideas.what: Predicted dichotomy: sections over S come from regular S-sections of U_S (integral points) or from K-rational cusps (sections of S' over S), with an open question of which cusps give non-empty packets of S-splittings.
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal sections / packets of cuspidal sections over a base
ideas.usually_credited_to: cuspidal sections over fields: Grothendieck, Nakamura, Stix (packets parametrised by Kummer classes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly poses determining when a K-rational cusp (a section of S' -> S) yields splittings of pi_1(U_S) -> pi_1(S), and describing all of them. The natural answer involves the cusp's normal bundle class in H^2(pi_1(S), Z^(1)) and units of O(S). The base-relative version of this cuspidal-packet question is not systematically treated, as far as I know.
missed.quote: il faudrait étudier encore à quelle condition une telle section définit un paquet non vide de scindages de (4) — et comment déterminer exactement tous ces scindages
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise, tractable question about cuspidal sections over higher-dimensional arithmetic bases, relevant to integral-point versions of the section conjecture. It is modest in scope.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine but clear spreading-out of the section conjecture over a model S. This viewpoint is folklore and is present in Stix's work. The only somewhat specific unpublished element is the question, continued on the next page, of which cusps give S-unramified splittings.
transcription_corrections: 'de noyau π_U' is probably 'de noyau π_{\bar U}' or simply π. The handwriting shows π with a subscript, consistent with the geometric fundamental group.
In 'ceux qui sont {+triviaux+} [-...-] sur le noyau', 'triviaux' is written above a struck-out word. The sense is 'trivial on the kernel of E_K -> E_S'.
Inside the square (5) there is a small mark (resembling '≈' or a fibre-product symbol) indicating that the square is cartesian. The transcription omits it.
'(disons, d'une certaine condition)' is uncertain; it may read 'disons, de type fini, satisfaisant une certaine condition'.
